card: This pull request speeds up descriptor parsing for descriptors containing extended public and private keys. The parser previously called both DecodeExtKey and DecodeExtPubKey on each extended key, redundantly running Base58Check and double-SHA256 passes twice per key, while descriptor checksums performed linear charset scans. This PR combines the key decodes into a single Base58Check pass, replaces checksum charset lookups with a 256-byte table, and switches Base58 string APIs to std::string_view. The author reports a 29.4% parsing speedup on a large multisig descriptor in microbenchmarks.
changed_since_previous: The Base58 decoding helper now caps the initial buffer allocation size using `max_ret_len - zeroes`.
evidence: Author provides microbenchmark results parsing a large multisig Taproot descriptor showing parse time reduced from 127,812 ns/op to 90,253 ns/op (~29.4% speedup) (PR description).
problem: When parsing extended keys, the descriptor parser unconditionally called both `DecodeExtKey()` and `DecodeExtPubKey()`, executing two separate Base58Check passes (including double-SHA256 hashing) even though only one prefix could match. In addition, descriptor checksumming performed linear scans over the character set for every character, and key decoding functions required `const std::string&`, causing redundant heap allocations and slowing down wallet fuzzing and descriptor parsing.

risk.why: A flaw in Base58 decoding or extended key parsing could cause valid descriptors or keys to be rejected or parsed incorrectly by the wallet.

summary: Improves descriptor parsing performance by combining extended key decoding (`xpub`/`xprv`) into a single Base58Check decode pass. It also replaces the O(N) linear character scan in descriptor checksum computation with a precomputed 256-byte lookup table, and updates Base58 and key decoding APIs to accept `std::string_view` to avoid string allocations.
